summary: Built a small Node.js LangChain-style lead scoring sample that reads lead data from an Azure DocumentDB cluster, uses an LLM to produce a 0-100 score and one-paragraph rationale (LLM call guarded), and writes the score + rationale back to the lead document. The repository includes an idempotent seed script, Express HTTP endpoint POST /score-lead, a CLI, unit test for the prompt builder, and documentation. I verified dependency installation, seeding, collection/index creation, data reads, and unit tests. I was not able to run an end-to-end scoring run because OPENAI_API_KEY was not present in the environment, so the LLM call and the final DB update via the agent were not executed here.
how_to_run:
1) Copy .env.example -> .env and fill DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY (if you want to enable the LLM).
2) npm install
3) npm run seed   # idempotent: creates database sample_customer_360_09, collections and indexes, and seed docs
4) npm test       # runs jest unit test
5a) npm run score # CLI run (defaults to lead-1), requires OPENAI_API_KEY to perform scoring
5b) npm start     # start Express server on port 3000; POST /score-lead with JSON {"leadId":"lead-1"}

Notes:
- DOCUMENTDB_URI must point to your Azure DocumentDB (mongoClusters) cluster and use SCRAM/TLS credentials. The code reads DB name from DB_NAME env (defaults to sample_customer_360_09).
- Do not commit secrets. Use secret store or env vars for OPENAI_API_KEY/DOCUMENTDB_URI.
- If you don't set OPENAI_API_KEY, you can still run the seed, tests, and data-inspection steps; the LLM call in the agent is guarded and will throw a clear error if attempted without a key.

documentdb MCP: documentdb_list_indexes enumerated indexes for activities, engagement_signals, leads (indexes created as expected)
fetchLeadContext call: programmatically retrieved lead context for lead-1 (activities and signals counts printed)
npm test (jest): passed (test for buildPrompt passed)

HTTP endpoint POST /score-lead full run (includes LLM call and DB update): not executed for the same reason as above
Any vector/embedding index creation and vector search: intentionally not implemented and not verified (design choice to avoid embedding complexity for this sample)
open_issues: OPENAI_API_KEY missing in the current environment — cannot verify LLM call or complete an end-to-end scoring run. Provide a valid key in .env to run end-to-end.

The sample intentionally omits embeddings/vector indexes to keep the sample focused on agent tooling + DocumentDB. If you want vector search included, add an embedding provider, create vector indexes (cosmosSearch with cosmosSearchOptions), and modify seed/agent accordingly.
